rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm §17 prevents: a narrated plan/explanation eats the student's top-of-response attention before the real content (a plan-mode item list, a numbered action) lands. §17's own mandatory-suppressor trigger is 'prompt with 4+ named sub-steps OR invokes plan mode' — Prompt 2 has 3 sub-steps, Prompt 3 has 2, neither invokes plan mode, so the trigger never fires and no suppressor/primer is owed. Closest line: curriculum/prompts/ae101-prework-extract-and-install.md:28 'I'm starting a training called Agentic Engineering 101. Walk these in order, ask one question at a time if you need to, no preamble.' — the scene-setting clause is what the behavior catalog flags as a med-confidence preamble invite, but it stays inside §17 because (a) the rule's mandatory trigger doesn't reach a 3-step mechanical setup and (b) a voluntary 'no preamble' clause is already present in the same sentence. No teaching moment rides on this prompt's opening line either way (mechanical extract/install, not a plan-mode reveal).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: **Overwrite anxiety — name overwrite default on regeneration.**
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm §16 prevents: Claude pauses to ask overwrite-or-new on a regeneration prompt, student picks 'create new' defensively, produces version-soup (agent.md + agent-v2.md). Present here? curriculum/prompts/ae101-prework-extract-and-install.md:30 ('Ensure my AE101 content directory exists... Create it if necessary') and the Step-3 skill install name no overwrite behavior, but per the fresh-install-context carve-out (memory/compounded/2026-05-24-prompts-overwrite-anxiety-fresh-install-carveout.md) this is curriculum-delivered first-bundle-encounter prework, not a regeneration of a student-authored artifact — the collision-pause path is not the modal case, so the harm §16 is built to prevent (version-soup on an evolving artifact) has no artifact to apply to.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: **Self-report + self-audit charity — verify at artifact, over-flag or fresh-session for critique.**
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm §31(a) prevents: Claude's summary inflates what actually happened (claims N sharpened when fewer were touched), and the student never opens the artifact to check. Present here? Prompts 2 and 3 both close with 'Report success on each step and tell me what you did,' but each named step already carries the exact falsifiable check the rule's own fix prescribes — closest line: curriculum/prompts/ae101-prework-extract-and-install.md:39 'Confirm each installed skill has a SKILL.md file and tell me the absolute path.' The summary rides on a named path/subfolder/test-status fact, not an ungrounded self-grade, so it stays inside.

Harm §32(a) prevents: an offered default (rules, structure) gets taken verbatim ~90% of the time, defeating an articulation goal the exercise is built around. Present here? curriculum/prompts/ae101-prework-extract-and-install.md:30 'Use ~/Documents/ae101-content unless there is a good reason not to' is an unscrutinized default, but it is a directory-naming convention with no articulation goal riding on it — the Artefact-contracts table at prework.md:112 treats this exact path as the stable identifier every later module keys off, so the 'default' is the intended canonical convention, not a stand-in for a customization step the rule expects the student to do.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: **Question-dump default — `in turn` too soft; two legal shapes.**
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm §15 prevents: Claude posts every question/criterion in one message, batch rhythm collapses, student answers two and skims the rest. Present here? curriculum/prompts/ae101-prework-screen-and-ready.md:23 names four screening criteria in one sentence — risk-shaped on its face — but legal shape (b), the body callout, is satisfied twice over: prework.md:62 (pre-prompt) names the failure mode ('dumps all four criteria at once') and the recovery ('One bug at a time, then the next'); prework.md:66 (post-prompt) names the AskUserQuestion tool plus a one-at-a-time alternative and hands the student the choice ('Whichever reads better'). Prompt 4 (one-at-a-time.md) operationalizes that recovery directly. Two independent legal shapes covering the same risk is over-covered, not under-covered.
